newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 17.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, March 17.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Shares greeted the long-awaited announcement of the country's election date with little excitement, looking instead to Wall Street for direction and closing lower as the Dow tumbled. The FTSE 100 index ended near the day's lows at 4,373.3, down 51.0.

FRANKFURT - Shares closed slightly lower in bourse trade as the softer dollar meant they were unable to follow the post-bourse rally that occurred on Friday after Wall Street moved to higher levels. The DAX-30 index of leading German shares closed 8.30 points down at 3,350.99 in early dealings. The IBIS DAX electronic trading system, on which Friday's rally had materialised, meanwhile lost 67.18 points to 3,337.11.

PARIS - Stocks finished sharply lower, mirroring falls in the dollar and bond prices due to worries that U.S. interest rates are headed higher. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 57.24 points, or 2.16 percent, at 2,588.38.

ZURICH - An easing U.S. dollar and widespread insecurity about the U.S. and European interest rate developments soured sentiment in the Swiss share market, leading to a close below the 4,600 point level on the blue-chip index. The blue-chip SMI index fell 79.7 points to 4,556.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 42.02 points to 2,891.84.

TOKYO - Stocks ended higher after clawing back late in the session to recoup early morning gains. Brokers said market direction was vague and the rises were brought on by bargain-hunting and buy-backs of shares which had been sold off lately. The Nikkei 225 closed 129.86 points higher at 18,053.50.

HONG KONG - A rebound in the property sector swept stocks to a firm close after heavy losses registered last week. The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 102.00 points, or 0.80 percent, at 12,838.53. But turnover fell to HK$9.11 billion from HK$12.52 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - Political instability in Papua New Guinea hit the shares of companies with links to the country but the overall market, particularly banks, closed firm after a bounce on Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index gained 4.2 points to 2,427.4.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended up in a day ruled by futures-related trade ahead of the contract close-out deadline. Hectic futures activity dominated trade in the morning session of trade ahead of the close-out at noon. Industrials shot up on futures play and golds were knocked down. But trade quietened down in the afternoon and the market moved sideways. The golds index fell 20.9 points to 1,387.8. The overall index ended up 3.9 points to 7,131.0 points and the industrial index added 53.4 points to 8,380.6 points.
